Selected personally by the lead under the user's instruction; assigned scalafim-umvpa-foundation-lead and tagged umvpa-lead-owned. Rationale: incorrect provider/lifecycle/semantic boundaries would propagate into nearly every delegated implementation. M0.01 remains an actual prerequisite; admission is not claimed while its ownership/deletion contract is open.

Initial read-only evidence: ScalaFIM build.sbt pins Gale 099832ff15c8a4a8fcf3398c7b779fb4bbc12434 and Multivar c4329fc95688929236c942cca889aa67ad17cbe0, but has no Alder or resample4s source pin. Local Alder HEAD 38c8cc8ef74f578a8ec008db8d09bad0a913a6fc has a clean build.sbt and hard-coded development sibling builds for ../resample4s, ../gale and ../linop4s; this was checked against git show HEAD:build.sbt, not inferred from memory. Local resample4s HEAD is 6bc4172a966c92f1b06811eac64ac2bada9fef9b; local Multivar HEAD 50da9087993e11922adeca570b1694079771b7a6 differs from ScalaFIM's admitted pin. These are source observations, not remote availability, successful consumer compilation or candidate admission.

Implementation must establish an immutable dependency closure and exact consumer JVM/JS evidence; simply pointing ScalaFIM at the mutable sibling Alder build is not sufficient. Do not silently use the newer local Multivar API to justify the existing pin. Next: after M0.01 contracts settle, construct the bounded provider consumer spike, resolve any exact missing upstream admission capability, and then unlock M0.03. No tests or numerical qualification were run in this selection step.
